notes.claim: With a 100% rate over a period, simple interest doubles the money but continually compounding interest multiplies it by e.
e is a fixed constant like π, approximately 2.71828.
In exponential growth the rate of growth is proportional to the current value.

sources.title: 6.8 Exponential Growth and Decay - Calculus Volume 1 | OpenStax
sources.quote: That is, the rate of growth is proportional to the current function value.

sources.title: Answers and Explanations -- The Number $e$ as a Limit
sources.quote: Under simple interest alone, the money will double during that period. Under continually compounding interest, it will be multiplied by e.

sources.title: Euler Number (e) — Definition, Formula & Examples
sources.quote: e is a fixed constant like π . It always equals approximately 2.71828 and cannot be assigned a different value.
